author: egalli
title: ARM64 cross-compilation build fails with cc1plus: not a PCH file (invalid-pch) in openvino_reference
signature: cc1plus error cmake_pch hxx gch not a pch file werror invalid pch|Infrastructure

failed_jobs.name: Build / Build
failed_jobs.symptom: cmake --build fails compiling src/core/reference objects: cc1plus rejects the precompiled header (cmake_pch.hxx.gch) as 'not a PCH file' under -Werror=invalid-pch, stopping ninja with multiple FAILED entries.

failed_jobs.name: ci/gha_overall_status_ubuntu_22_arm64_cross_compilation
failed_jobs.symptom: Aggregate status-check job reports failure because the upstream Build job failed.

key_errors:
FAILED: [code=1] src/core/reference/CMakeFiles/openvino_reference.dir/src/op/convert.cpp.o
cc1plus: error: /__w/openvino/openvino/openvino/openvino_build/src/core/reference/CMakeFiles/openvino_reference.dir/cmake_pch.hxx.gch: not a PCH file [-Werror=invalid-pch]

FAILED: [code=1] src/core/reference/CMakeFiles/openvino_reference.dir/src/op/einsum.cpp.o
cc1plus: error: /__w/openvino/openvino/openvino/openvino_build/src/core/reference/CMakeFiles/openvino_reference.dir/cmake_pch.hxx.gch: not a PCH file [-Werror=invalid-pch]
ninja: build stopped: subcommand failed.
root_cause: The ARM64 cross-compilation build uses a precompiled header (cmake_pch.hxx.gch) for the openvino_reference target together with sccache as the compiler launcher. The sccache-cached/launched cc1plus invocation picks up a stale or incompatible .gch artifact (likely produced by a different compiler invocation/toolchain variant, or corrupted/truncated by a concurrent cache write) and rejects it as 'not a PCH file'. Because CMAKE_COMPILE_WARNING_AS_ERROR=ON turns the resulting -Winvalid-pch warning into a hard error, every translation unit in the openvino_reference target that consumes the shared PCH fails to compile, cascading into a full ninja build-stop. This is the 9th occurrence of the exact same signature recorded in the pattern database (6 occurrences in the last 12 hours alone), strongly indicating an infrastructure/toolchain-cache issue (sccache + PCH interaction on the ARM64 cross-compile runners) rather than anything introduced by this PR's MVN-6 axis-validation change, which does not touch build configuration, PCH settings, or any file in src/core/reference's compiled list.
reproduction_steps: Not reliably reproducible locally outside the ARM64 cross-compilation CI runners / sccache configuration. To attempt reproduction: configure with the same cmake-options as the job (-DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE=cmake/arm64.toolchain.cmake -DCMAKE_COMPILE_WARNING_AS_ERROR=ON -DENABLE_FASTER_BUILD=ON) using sccache as CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_LAUNCHER, build the openvino_reference target, and watch for a stale/truncated cmake_pch.hxx.gch under a warm sccache cache; clearing the sccache cache/precompiled-header artifact before build is the most likely way to force or avoid the symptom.
recommended_actions: Clear/invalidate the sccache cache (or the specific cached PCH artifact) for the ubuntu_22_04_arm64_cross_compile_Release key used by this job, since the .gch file is almost certainly stale or produced by an incompatible compiler invocation.

Consider disabling or relaxing -Werror=invalid-pch for this specific toolchain (cross-compilation + sccache), or disabling PCH (ENABLE_FASTER_BUILD/precompiled headers) for the openvino_reference target on ARM64 cross-compile until the sccache+PCH interaction is fixed, since this has now recurred 9 times.
Call remediate_transient_failure to re-run the failed jobs / re-queue the PR, since a clean (non-cached) rebuild is very likely to succeed.
File/escalate a tracking issue against the ARM64 cross-compilation CI config to investigate sccache compatibility with precompiled headers, given the high recurrence count.
prevention_strategies: Add a CI safeguard that detects PCH/sccache cache corruption (e.g., validate the .gch artifact's age/hash against the current compiler invocation before reuse) and automatically purges stale PCH caches. Alternatively, disable precompiled headers for cross-compilation targets where sccache is the launcher, since sccache does not natively understand PCH semantics and can serve a mismatched .gch file.
historical_context: This exact signature has now been recorded 9 times in the CI Doctor MQ pattern database (first seen 2026-09-24, most recently 6 times in the last 12 hours alone, across unrelated PRs #37942, #38030, #38380, #38393, #38483, #38604, #38607, #38611, and now #37908). All occurrences point to the same ARM64 cross-compilation 'Build / Build' job and the same cc1plus invalid-pch error in src/core/reference, confirming this is a persistent CI infrastructure issue unrelated to the specific PR content.
